title: Priests exploit offerings — 1 Samuel 2
paragraphs: In 1 Samuel 2, the priests were not outsiders mocking God. They were insiders handling sacred things while exploiting the people and dishonoring the Lord. They took what was not theirs. They abused worship for appetite. They stood near the altar, but their hearts were far from God.
That is the terror of hidden sin.

You can look spiritual.
Sound spiritual.
Serve in spiritual spaces.
And still treat what belongs to God like it exists for you.

But here’s what we miss: this story is not only about corrupt priests back then. It is a warning to every heart that uses ministry, position, gifting, or influence to feed the flesh. God sees what people excuse. He does not wink at sin dressed in religion.
Because where priests failed, Jesus did not.

He is the faithful High Priest — pure, undefiled, and incapable of exploiting the sheep. He does not steal from the altar. He became the sacrifice on it. He does not devour the people. He lays down His life for them. That means the answer to corrupted religion is not better performance. It is repentance and a return to Christ.

If you have mishandled holy things, come clean.
If you have used God’s name to hide compromise, repent.
If church wounds made you distrust spiritual leaders, look again at Jesus.

Men fail.
Systems fail.
Jesus does not.

1 Samuel 2 is brutal.
But it is also a mercy.
God exposes what sin wants to keep hidden — so grace can heal what pride tried to protect.
“Those who honor Me I will honor…” — 1 Samuel 2:30

Honor Him in secret.
Honor Him in your motives.
Honor Him when no one is clapping.
